body.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
body.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: a total uniformly calibrated test and an original fixed-\(n\), constant-null-supported converse must be proved on the identical class and optimized independently before any matching claim.
body.gap: At the revised stress separation, the exact \(2+1\) projection is controlled, but the same repeated fine-cell pair joined to three distinct fine-cell singletons has a fifth canonical projection whose squared \(L^2\) contribution grows as \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  A new cancellation or a direct Hellinger comparison, plus the matching upper concentration theorem and all-regime optimization, is still required.
body.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a bounded constant-null-supported prior whose fixed-sample comparison cancels or bypasses the exact \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection, or prove a direct Hellinger bound despite the divergent second likelihood moment; independently prove a uniformly calibrated multiresolution upper test from a deterministic alternative dichotomy and signal-dependent sparse-occupancy projection bounds, then optimize and compare the two repaired maps in every regime.
obligation.obstruction: For the mandated four-atom law, the \(2+1\) contribution is only \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\) at \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), but a repeated fine-cell pair together with three distinct fine-cell singletons in the same macro cube has exact fifth canonical projection \(\delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5\).  Its squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) contribution is at least \(c_b(n)_5h^dH^{3d}\delta^8\), which is \(c_b\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\) at \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), and \(H\asymp\delta\).  Therefore the proposed support-controlled chi-square connected remainder is not \(O(\epsilon^4)\).  This does not logically preclude a direct Hellinger comparison, but no such comparison follows from the frozen primitives or the computed likelihood projections.
obligation.attempted: The bounded four-atom probabilities, zero coordinate means, fixed squares, correlation shift, binary margins, Hölder bounds, exact uniform design, consistency, exchangeability, componentwise constant null CATE, alternative separation, one-observation matching, and distinct-fine matching were verified.  Möbius subtraction gave the exact \(2+1\) projection and showed it is controlled at the revised scale.  Extending the same exact likelihood algebra to a \(2+3\) occupancy produced the fifth canonical projection; core-volume counting and orthogonality over sample-coordinate subsets yielded the divergent lower bound.  No claim was made that chi-square divergence alone forces Hellinger divergence.
